title: Tokenized prompt indexing and cross-session reuse for KV cache
creator: Ava Reynolds
description: Problem: We observe repeated allocations of near-identical KV segments in GPU memory across concurrent requests and short-lived sessions. These duplicate KV blobs increase peak memory pressure, reduce effective batch sizes, and lead to more frequent kernel spills on 80GB/40GB cards. Goal: implement a tokenized prompt indexing layer that can canonicalize and fingerprint prompt prefixes across normalization differences, enabling safe cross-session reuse and deduplication of cached KV entries. The solution should be runtime-friendly (tight latency path for hits), privacy-aware (per-tenant salting / KMS-managed salts), and hardware-aware (hotset pinning and eviction policies tuned for GPU memory fragmentation). This ticket scopes the design and a pilot implementation integrated into continuous batching and KV lookup paths.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate KV memory footprint reduced by >= 35% on representative chat workload in staging (measured peak GPU usage for cached kv).
End-to-end median token generation latency unchanged or improved; p95 token latency not regressed by more than 5%.
Batching throughput increased by >= 12% on workload with repeated prefixes when dedupe is enabled.
Cross-session reuse path respects per-tenant salt and can be disabled per tenant via config.
Comprehensive unit and integration tests for canonicalization and hash collisions added.
Instrumentation dashboard (KV dedupe hit/miss, pinned set size, eviction churn) exists and is linked in the PR.
technical_notes: Canonicalization: apply model-agnostic normalizations (unicode NFKC, whitespace collapse, lowercasing configurable) before tokenization. Store both raw canonicalized string and tokenized run-length chunk signatures to support alignment across models.

Fingerprinting: compute content-addressable fingerprint over token-run windows with an HMAC using per-tenant salt retrieved from KMS to prevent cross-tenant inference attacks. Use 64-bit truncated Blake3 for compactness and speed; include version byte in key to allow rolling algorithm changes.

Index layout: central small-memory index (CPU) mapping fingerprint -> (gpu_shard, offset, length, model_variant_signature). The actual KV bytes live in GPU pinned pools; the index entry is compact to keep lookups CPU-cacheable.

Lookup path: on request, compute fingerprints for candidate prefix windows incrementally (O(n) streaming), issue a batched lookup to the index, and attach any found KV slices to the request's KV merge path. Optimize common-case 1-hit fast path to avoid extra allocations.

Eviction: size-aware LRU with frequency boost for 'hot pins'. When GPU fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation, fallback to split-slice placement plus a compact indirect lookup. Eviction hints propagated to batch scheduler to avoid prefetch storms.
Prefetch and warmup: track short-term access traces per route. For routes with stable hot prefixes, prefetch into pinned GPU pool during low-util periods and opportunistically during canary traffic.

Multi-model considerations: store model_variant_signature to ensure a fingerprint only reuses KV for compatible model architectures / kv layouts. Provide a lightweight compatibility function to allow reuse across quantization variants where safe.
Concurrency: implement atomic compare-and-link semantics for index insertion to avoid duplicate concurrent writes. Use per-shard write buffers and coalescing to reduce GPU upload contention.
Observability: emit metrics for fingerprint compute time, index lookup latency, dedupe hit ratio, memory reclaimed, failed validation count, and per-tenant dedupe enablement.

Security/privacy: per-tenant salt + KMS rotation; fingerprint metadata intentionally avoids storing plaintext prompt fragments. Provide an opt-out switch for regulated tenants where caching is disallowed.
milestones: 2026-03-10: Design doc and API sketch completed (this ticket).
2026-03-18: Implementation: index and fast lookup path + unit tests (ENG RFC).
2026-03-25: Integration: GPU pinned pool placement, eviction policy, and instrumentation wired to console dashboards.
2026-03-29: Staging load test and safety checks (privacy, collision detection).
2026-04-02: Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for routes flagged as safe; monitor and iterate.
testing_plan: Unit: canonicalization edge-cases, HMAC salt rotation, fingerprint collision simulation.
Integration: end-to-end serving with and without dedupe for chat and search workloads.
Load: synthetic mix with high prefix locality to validate memory saving and batch sizing improvements.
Chaos: forced GPU fragmentation tests to verify split-slice fallback and eviction correctness.
Privacy: verified no plaintext prefix storage in index and correct salt handling in logs.
rollout_plan: Feature gated: per-tenant flag default-off; enable for internal tenants and opt-in customers first.
Canary: 5% traffic for safe routes, monitor KV memory, generation latency, service errors for 72h.
Scale: gradually increase by factor of 2 every 24h if metrics stable, with automatic rollback thresholds on memory pressure or error rate.
Post-rollout: run 2-week measurement window to quantify billable token cost improvements and update Optimize recommendations.
